concepts.description: 416 BC. *"The standard of justice depends on the equality of power to compel… the strong do what they have the power to do and the weak accept what they have to accept"*, and *"a general and necessary law of nature to rule whatever one can."* ⚠ **Filed as TRANSGRESSION — the error illustrated is the Melians'.** Athens is *"eminently practical"*; the killing of every man of military age, the enslavement of the women and children and the recolonisation of the island get one sentence, as the outcome of the victims' pride. **Documented, not smoothed.** ⚠ **Thucydides is never named** — a historian's reconstruction is presented as transcribed speech from 416 BC. ⚠ **Greene's one real argument** — that the leadership spent the lives of *"a lot of people who do not believe in your cause"* — gets a single clause and cuts both ways. ⚠ **The counterfactual is unsupported and load-bearing**: no evidence that a subject Melos could have sabotaged anything or left the alliance

concepts.title: Brecht Before the HUAC
concepts.description: 30 October 1947. **Five separable techniques**: the suit he rarely wore, the cigar chosen because the chairman smoked them, one completely true answer to the only question that mattered (he was not a Party member), total deference — and **an interpreter used throughout despite adequate English, as a device for producing a second softer text with someone else's name on it.** *"No, I wrote a German poem, which is very different from this."* **The evasions were protected by the deference; either alone fails.** ⚠ **Greene concedes the lies** — *"outright lies that went unchallenged because they were wrapped in enigmas."* ⚠ **The comparison with the Hollywood 19 is not like-for-like**: Greene admits they *"gained a kind of vindication"*, and Brecht preserved a working freedom he left the country the next day to avoid using — he was leaving anyway. ⚠ The technique is calibrated to institutions that must be seen to be fair

concepts.title: Hotta Masayoshi and the Soft Invasion
concepts.description: the 1857 memorandum, **the best-sourced item in the chapter and still uncited**: alliances, trade, *"copy the foreigners where they are at their best and so repair our own shortcomings"*, complete our armaments, *"and so gradually subject the foreigners to our influence."* **The copying is the hard part** — it requires a governing class to state publicly that the rival is better, which is the proposal most likely to end a career in 1857. **The mechanism is real: *"the enemy has nothing to react against, prepare for, or resist."*** ⚠ **Greene's paraphrase converts an imperial programme into a defensive one** — the document ends at *"our hegemony is acknowledged throughout the globe,"* dressed as universal tranquillity. ⚠ *"Inwardly maintain your own culture"* has no mechanism at state scale: the institution meant to hold the interior is staffed a generation later by the people the copying produced. ⚠ No outcome evidence after 1857 is offered at all

concepts.title: Goujian in the Stables of Wu
concepts.description: 473 BC, after Fujiao. **The decision is flight versus proximity, not fight versus yield** — he wanted to run; the adviser sent him into his conqueror's stables as the lowest servant *"from which position he could study the man and plot his revenge."* **Distance is safety and nothing else; proximity is danger plus information.** ⚠ **The exit condition belongs to the deceived party** — three years, ending when the ruler was *"finally satisfied of his loyalty"* — so the term was open-ended, which is the strategy's largest unpriced cost. ⚠ **A drought and inner turmoil delivered the victory.** Surrender kept him present and informed until an external shock arrived; it produced no opening of its own. ⚠ The interior was held by a revenge plot maintained at working temperature for a thousand days

concepts.title: Voltaire and the London Mob
concepts.description: *(Pass 6)* surrounded by a crowd shouting *"Hang the Frenchman"*: *"Men of England! You wish to kill me because I am a Frenchman. Am I not punished enough in not being born an Englishman?"* **He concedes the premise entirely and extends it past where the crowd had taken it** — out-arguing them by agreeing harder — and hands a hostile English mob a compliment they could not have extracted by force. They cheered and escorted him home. ⚠ **It buys no time and needs none**, so the law's central mechanism is absent from one of its own cases. ⚠ **Distinct on three axes** from everything else in the chapter: instantaneous, verbal rather than postural, and aimed at a temporary formation with no memory and no capacity to verify. ⚠ Sourced to *The Little, Brown Book of Anecdotes*, Fadiman ed., 1985 — an anecdote collection, `[PLAUSIBLE — needs corroboration]`

concepts.title: Arnold, Slack and the Salted Diamond Mine
concepts.description: $12,000 of European gems salted into Wyoming, twice. **Every expert was real, every check was honest, and Janin — *"a born skeptic"* — dug for eight days and called it *"the richest field in mining history."*** ⚠ **The mark funded the deception**: Ralston's $100,000 security payment bought the Amsterdam sacks used for the second salting, and Greene reports both halves without connecting them. ⚠ **The endorsement cascade is the real engine** — *"anyone who doubted it was questioning the intelligence of the world's most successful businessmen"* — so the vanity exploited in the mark also recruits the mark as the con's security system. Stated once, never generalised. ⚠ **Not one check tested the ground the stones came out of.** ⚠ Harpending ruined; Slack vanished; **Arnold went home to Kentucky, enlarged his farm and opened a bank**, because *"his sale of his mining rights had been legitimate"* — Arnold's defence, reported in Greene's voice with no distance marked

concepts.title: Bismarck and the Game of Quinze
concepts.description: 1865, a treaty *"totally in the interests of Prussia and against the interests of Austria."* **The target was not the man but his announced diagnostic method** — Blome *"often said"* he judged character by quinze, and Bismarck fed the instrument, losing several thousand talers deliberately. ⚠ **The deception is in the inference, not the trait**: Bismarck genuinely was aggressive, the reputation was accurate, the card play *confirmed a true thing*, and Blome supplied *aggressive → rash → incapable of cold calculation* himself — **so there was no false statement to catch.** ⚠ **What was purchased was inattention** — Blome believed his diligence was complete, so *"he only glanced at the treaty before signing it."* ⚠ **The gloat violates the law**: revealing the trick to Blome's face immediately converts a repeatable asset into one win, and Greene reports it as the punchline. Bismarck's method here is the same as at Law 19's weak king — controlling the perception of the one person whose perception decides

concepts.title: Isabella d'Este and the Survival of Mantua
concepts.description: forty years holding Mantua between France, Venice, Rome and Milan, run on four simultaneous tracks: a husband sent to fight for the pope *"knowing he would not fight very hard"*, French troops let through her territory, a public complaint of invasion, and **a staged French plunder of her own city** to make the complaint survive inspection. Cesare Borgia *"could be neither trusted nor in any way offended"* — managed with falcons, perfumes, **dozens of masks because she knew what he wore when he did not want to be recognised**, a godfathership for her own child, and messengers who doubled as spies. ⚠ **The flagship case for standing back never stands back** — she is inside every fray, on every side. ⚠ She was neutral **between her own husband and her own brother**, and Greene reports it without remark. ⚠ **The preconditions are never stated**: a duchy, a court, an army-owning husband, and a room where Leonardo built the decorations. Mantua's sovereignty held a century past her death in 1539

concepts.title: Castruccio and the Two Gates of Pistoia
concepts.description: two armies, two gates, two hostile factions who each welcomed theirs in. **He kept both promises literally** — *"And Castruccio kept his promises"* — and **the betrayal is in the *scope* of the promise, not its truth**, which is deception without a lie and a category the book does not have. **The town's own defensive infrastructure was the entry point, operated by its own people, on purpose.** ⚠ *"Killed the leaders of both factions, ended the internal war"* — the pacification is listed as one of four accomplishments, in sequence, with no pause. ⚠ **He does not run the law he illustrates**: the chapter is about staying out of fights and he enters one twice, on both sides, with troops. ⚠ He also ignores the timing rule two paragraphs earlier — he collects while both factions are still standing

concepts.title: Washington and the Refusal of Alliance
concepts.description: *"a treaty with France might have helped in the short term"* traded away because **the help and the status could not both be accepted: accepting the help is the statement.** The refusal has to be *witnessed* to pay, which is why Greene says *trumpet* — **the one case in the law where the audience is the point.** ⚠ **This passage reverses the Keys to Power six paragraphs above it** (*"you cannot completely stand aside"* → *"drop all pretence of appearing supportive"*), marked only by *"there are occasions when"*, with no criterion. ⚠ Greene calls it a *"pose"* and aims it at *"those who need to gain respect"* — **the chapter's only address to a reader without standing**, illustrated by a head of state. ⚠ The closing payoff is *"a position of power from which you can choose to help others"* — a gentler destination than the chapter earns. ⚠ No dates, no treaty named, no Farewell Address: `[LOW CONFIDENCE]` on the historical account as given

concepts.title: Talleyrand at the Window, 1830
concepts.description: *"Ah, the bells! We're winning." / "Who's 'we,' mon prince?" / "Not a word! I'll tell you who we are tomorrow."* **The pronoun arrives before the allegiance** — he identifies with the winner while not yet knowing who won, and gives himself one night. ⚠ **The risk is not his uncertainty but the witness to it**: the shush is the load-bearing move, because a spoken not-knowing becomes a public position. ⚠ **Greene's gloss does not fit his own scene** — he explains it through *"people also respect you less"*, a claim about public reputation, in an anecdote about successfully keeping something private. ⚠ **The cheapest case in the chapter**: Isabella's version took forty years, Huan's needed an army, this needed him to not say a sentence. Fourth Talleyrand page in the vault; the book contains a complete portrait of one operator and never draws it

concepts.title: Elizabeth I and the Virgin Queen Strategy
concepts.description: an unmade marriage held open for twenty-five years as the country's principal diplomatic instrument. **The courtship *was* the payment**: France received a plausible prospect of the English throne entering its royal house, England received a signed peace, and the prospect was reclaimed the moment the treaty existed. **An expectation is the only asset that can be delivered to several parties simultaneously and reclaimed at no cost.** Mary Queen of Scots is the controlled comparison — same structural position, commits, and loses — with two distinct failure mechanisms named: **entanglement** and **displacement** (Darnley did attempt it). ⚠ Greene converts the instrument into a goal (*"two goals as a ruler: to avoid marriage and to avoid war"*), which inverts the causation his own evidence supports. ⚠ The heir problem is conceded in a subordinate clause — the strategy **deferred the succession crisis past her death** rather than solving it. ⚠ And the cult output (Forman's diary, Spenser's eulogies, *"that virtuous Virgo"*) is **the same apotheosis as Deioces at Law 16 by a different withholding** — sustained denial produces worship, not frustration, and neither chapter says so. `[CONTESTED]`

concepts.title: Kissinger and Both 1968 Campaigns
concepts.description: inside information supplied to Nixon **and** to Humphrey, *"I've hated Nixon for years"* said to the Democrats, and a cabinet post secured from both. ⚠ **The chapter cannot distinguish withholding from manufacturing**: Elizabeth made no false statements and Kissinger manufactured two false impressions — the first cannot be discovered, the second can, and Greene files them together. **What protected him was structural, not skill: he chose a service the buyer could not admit to receiving**, so the only two parties able to expose him would each have had to confess first. ⚠ On surviving the 1972 purge and Watergate — **a committed man is *usable as a gesture*** and an uncommitted one has nothing to signal by being sacrificed; Greene reads survival as vindication of judgement. ⚠ **Sixth Kissinger appearance in this build and still one method** (Laws 2, 3, 4, 7, 9, 20): *never occupying a position that can be taken from you.* `[CONTESTED]` — the claim that Humphrey also promised a post is the strongest and least supported element

concepts.title: Alcibiades and the Three Cities
concepts.description: Athens, Sparta, Persia; promises to each and commitment to none. **The operative move is the second defection: he left Sparta *while Sparta was rising*** — not a bet on Persia but **maintenance**, since the moment he settles anywhere he stops being a bridge and becomes an asset of whoever holds him. ⚠ **His entire holding was three parties' beliefs about his standing with the other two** — costless to hold, impossible for any of them to verify, and **destroyed by use**, because an exercised influence becomes a measured one and every measured influence is smaller than an imagined one. ⚠ **Greene ends at *"he held all the cards"*** and omits the recall to Athens, the renewed loss of confidence, and the murder in Phrygia — an ending that follows directly from an asset that cannot be converted. ⚠ Greene's own verb gives it away: *"you will immediately **seem** a person of great influence."* Ultimately Thucydides and Plutarch, neither cited. `[CONTESTED]`

concepts.title: Norfleet and the Denver Con Ring
concepts.description: the Texas cattleman who lost $45,000 and spent five years, his solvency and his marriage destroying the largest con confederation in America; two of the men turned themselves in rather than keep being hunted. ⚠ **The case does not fit the type it illustrates.** Greene files him as the Hopelessly Insecure Man, who *"will attack you in bites that will take forever to get big enough for you to notice"* — and Norfleet declared his intention in one sentence to the police and ran a five-year public campaign. **The typology has no cell for undeterrable, public and effective.** ⚠ The real lesson is variance, not psychology: **Furey's model was right about the average mark and fatal about the tail**, and the ring's connectedness converted one outlier into total loss. A hundred silent victims does not make the hundred-and-first more likely to be silent — it only increases what there is to lose. ⚠ Also records the cost column Greene includes and the frame has no room for: the mortgaged ranch, the collapsed marriage, and a wife who ran the ranch for five years

concepts.title: Lope de Aguirre and the Three-Year Pursuit
concepts.description: 200 lashes avenged across more than a thousand leagues on foot over three years and four months, and the murderer who walked back in for his forgotten hat. **He enforced the verdict on himself for the whole duration** — no horse, unseen, barefoot, *"a whipped man has no business to ride a horse"* — which is why the pursuit outlasted any emotion. **The humiliation did not produce anger, it produced a new self-description, and descriptions do not decay.** ⚠ Esquivel's three defences (distance, jurisdiction, personal precaution) were all competent and all **calibrated to an opponent doing a cost-benefit calculation**; none addresses someone whose cost function has stopped having alternatives in it. ⚠ Filed under the Proud Man's *"vengeance of overwhelming violence"* and exhibits the Serpent's patience with the Proud Man's trigger — a combination the typology has no cell for. ⚠ Documented per standing practice: the enslaved Indians whose overburdening caused the arrest appear in the first sentence and never again. Named source chain (Walker Chapman 1967, quoting Garcilaso de la Vega)

concepts.title: Chung-erh and the Ruler of Cheng
concepts.description: the minister's advice given as a **dilemma with both branches named** — *place him under an obligation*, or *put him to death to avoid calamity in the future* — and ignored on both. ⚠ **Greene reads a forecasting error; the text shows a perception error**: the ruler was *"able to see only the prince's lowly station"* and had not registered the man as a subject at all, which is why he could take neither branch. **Both require taking the stranger seriously.** ⚠ Shu Chan's rule is **Machiavelli's *caressed or annihilated* from Law 15**, thirteen centuries earlier and four laws later in the book, with the same forbidden middle — and Greene prints both without noticing he has a principle rather than two anecdotes. **The rule is better than the typology because it requires no classification at all.** ⚠ Fourth adviser in this build who was correct and unheeded

concepts.title: Shih Huang Ti and the 270 Pavilions
concepts.description: secret passageways, a different bedroom every night, beheading for accidental sight of him, and a corpse carried home behind a cart of salted fish. ⚠ **The fortress is step four, not step one**: the Confucian proscription manufactured enemies, which produced fear, which produced executions, which produced more enemies, which produced the withdrawal. **Greene blames step four.** ⚠ And the withdrawal reduced not the number of people who could kill him but **the number who could protect him**, while raising the payoff to whoever inside acted — with Greene's own clause conceding he was *"probably poisoned by the same scheming ministers who encouraged his isolation."* If the isolation was advised, this is a manipulation filed as a lesson about circulation. `[CONTESTED]` on the book-burning and the poisoning — much of it derives from later Han sources with an interest in blackening the Ch'in

concepts.title: Versailles as Surveillance Architecture
concepts.description: the *lever* as an instrument of government: a hundred people admitted to a bedroom in a fixed order of rank, and Saint-Simon on the four words that ended a career — *"I do not know him."* **Louis did not build a place to observe from; he built one where privacy was impossible *including for himself*** and put his bedroom at the centre. **The nobility were policed by each other**, because standing was relative and visible, which makes the system self-administering. **Ambition was redirected rather than suppressed** onto prizes that are infinitely divisible, worthless outside the palace, and free to mint. ⚠ Flags that Versailles satisfies three of Machiavelli's four objections to a fortress, so the law's real content is *do not build one with private rooms*; and that Greene's success criterion is *unchallenged* — fifty years of peace and an aristocracy trained out of every competence except precedence, the same criterion applied at Visconti's court in Law 17

concepts.title: Cicero and Talleyrand as Circulators
concepts.description: **the only non-rulers in the law, and the only two the law's stated advice actually fits** (Louis never went anywhere; he made everyone come to him). Cicero mapped not just who had influence but **how they were connected to one another** — the edges, which is what makes counterbalancing possible. Talleyrand solved the opposite problem downward, into criminal Paris, and survived four regime changes. **A network built inside an institution expires with the institution; one built across institutions survives them.** ⚠ Flags the cost the chapter hides — circulation is not the absence of an expensive strategy but a different one, paid in small continuous instalments, which is why it is abandoned exactly when it matters most. ⚠ And Cicero built this network and was ultimately proscribed and killed; **Greene stops before the ending**

concepts.title: Fischer versus Spassky, Reykjavik 1972
concepts.description: the endless pre-conditions, a deliberate first-game blunder, a forfeited second game, and a man who had never lost control X-raying the chairs and finding two dead flies in a lighting fixture. **Spassky named the mechanism correctly before a move was played and lost anyway.** ⚠ Greene's stated thesis cannot explain the outcome: if the contest were about denying a reader material, **the superior psychologist should have adapted** — and Greene himself calls Spassky the better psychologist. What defeated him was a stakes asymmetry no amount of skill converts. ⚠ Also flags that the case is graded by its result: Greene's own text preserves *"rattled? Unsettled? Even, as some thought, insane?"*, and identical conduct after a loss in game three reads as breakdown. Third instance of the sorting-by-outcome defect after Napoleon (L8) and Lola Montez

concepts.title: Filippo Maria Visconti and the Oscillating Favour
concepts.description: **the law's purest mechanism and its least famous case.** Attention, then disdain; the courtier prepares to leave and is recalled; he adjusts to expecting nothing and is rebuked for lack of ambition. **All four postures punished** — and the reversals are triggered by the courtier's *own conclusions*, which is why effort cannot escape it. Greene's stated survival strategy is a list of things to stop doing: do not presume, do not guess, never inject your will, wait. **That is not obedience — obedience still requires knowing what is wanted.** The product is the surrender of independent judgement, and the chapter counts an unchallenged court as an unqualified win. ⚠ **The mechanism does not require intent**: ordinary inconsistency produces an identical experience from below. `[LOW CONFIDENCE]` — reported as habitual practice with an unnamed courtier's reasoning narrated as fact

concepts.title: Deioces and the Withdrawal from Judgment
concepts.description: the Mede who became the country's sole arbiter, quit at the peak, and was begged to be king. **The case contains two withdrawals doing opposite jobs and the law has one category for them**: the first *manufactures demand* and requires an audience to notice; the second — walls, messengers, one audience a week — *prevents evaluation* and requires them never to see enough to conclude anything. Herodotus supplies the mechanism, quoted by name: *"if nobody saw him, the legend would grow that he was a being of a different order from mere men."* **Absence does not make people admire you; it removes the material they would use to measure you.** ⚠ Two invisible preconditions do enormous work — he was genuinely good, and the alternative courts were corrupt, so there was **no acceptable substitute**. Greene reads a substitutability story as a scarcity story. ⚠ And Law 16 calls his walls the *"ultimate realization"* of the law while **Law 18 spends a chapter calling the identical architecture fatal**; neither chapter references the other

concepts.title: Guillaume de Balaun and the Manufactured Quarrel
concepts.description: the troubadour who staged a rupture in order to experience reconciliation. **The technique succeeded completely and the operator experienced the success as a loss** — his absence produced devotion rather than anger, and devotion freely offered is exactly what makes reconciliation impossible. **He was trying to extract a by-product**: reconciliation feels as it does because the danger was real, so manufacturing the danger yields either no danger or real danger, with no third setting. What finally delivered the sensation was a year of *involuntary* absence, a poem, and a fingernail sent as penance — none of it planned. ⚠ Filed under a law about deliberate withdrawal, and **the deliberate withdrawal fails twice.** Also flags that the operator was inside the mechanism he was operating: her pursuit lowered his estimate of her, so by the time it resolved he no longer wanted what he had engineered. Source is the Occitan *razo* tradition, uncited, and plausibly reverse-engineered from the surviving poem

concepts.title: Hsiang Yu and the Four Spared Escapes
concepts.description: *(reslugged from `hsiang-yu-and-liu-pang` per the Pass 5 verdict, to avoid sitting one keystroke from the existing Sawyer page)*. Four escapes granted to one man, with the outcome correctly predicted by Fan Tseng after the first. **The error was not mercy but declaring an intention and failing to complete it** — from the botched sword dance onward Liu had certainty about the game while Hsiang kept the ambivalence, so every Liu decision was clean and every Hsiang decision had to be re-argued. *"If you insist on boiling your own father, send me a bowl of the soup"* — **the fraternal bond was a lever Liu could pull, not merely a shield he sheltered under.** ⚠ Flags that Greene names the real motive (*"force his former friend to acknowledge him as master"*) in a subordinate clause and then attributes the behaviour to sentiment; that the *"a bit dull witted"* characterisation is refuted by Hsiang beheading his own commanding officer in the same chapter; and that the material is Sima Qian's *Shiji*, uncited

concepts.title: Empress Wu Chao
concepts.description: the harem, the royal urinal, the convent, the edict, and the newborn smothered minutes after the empress's visit. Forty years on the throne, and **the law's only case where the policy was actually run to completion over a long horizon.** ⚠ The conditions are never stated and they are load-bearing: a **closed system** with an enumerable roster of rivals, all of them heirs — against Greene's own Versailles counter-case twenty lines later, where crushing manufactured an opposition that had not existed. **She removed three of her own sons to install a figurehead**, which is *manufacturing a weak counterparty* rather than eliminating a strong one, and the book has no name for it. Also flags that Greene's structural argument (no route to power was open to an ambitious woman) undercuts his strategic conclusion, and that this flagship observance does not obey the law's own closing limit. `[CONTESTED]` on the infanticide

concepts.title: Cesare Borgia at Sinigaglia
concepts.description: the condottieri's trap turned inside out. **The first move was not an attack — it was Michelotto taking the canal bridge**, closing withdrawal before anyone knew a fight was happening; then the effusive greeting, the quiet arrest indoors, the simultaneous destruction outside, and the throttling last. **Completeness was an output of sequencing, not of resolve**, which is the dial Law 15 does not have. ⚠ The public execution of Ramiro de Lorca concealed the extraction that preceded it, and the confession's reliability is never examined — it happened to be right and could not have been known to be. **The chapter's only named, dated source (Ivan Cloulas, *The Borgias*, 1989, citing Machiavelli and Paolo Giovio) and it is marginal — sixth instance of the build's inverse-typography finding**

concepts.title: Chosroes II and the Loyalty Test
concepts.description: the king tells one courtier in confidence that his friend is a traitor and will be killed, then watches. **Both branches were scored before the trigger was pulled**: silence buys promotion and a cover story, disclosure buys banishment from the kingdom. **The test destroys one innocent per run by design** — the second courtier, who did nothing, reacted correctly to news of his own murder and is banished anyway, told he has done nothing wrong. *Knowledge is treated as contamination rather than as fault.* And what it selects for is not loyalty but **willingness to let a friend walk to a scaffold rather than break a confidence.** ⚠ The instrument can detect disloyalty and can never certify its absence, so it has **no terminal state** — which is the mechanism by which court paranoia becomes permanent rather than episodic. Also flags that the case does not fit its own law: it is run downward from a throne and depends entirely on the power to banish, the one resource the book's assumed reader lacks

concepts.title: Disinformation and the V-1 Bombs
concepts.description: turned agents feeding *"subtly deceptive information"* until the bombs *"were landing on cows in the country."* **The bombs walked rather than jumped, and the reason is a constraint not a preference**: each correction had to be plausible against the last, so credibility caps the correction rate. The Germans were not short of information — granular, timely, trusted — they simply had one source of depth and the enemy held it. Greene's image is exact: *"disinformation puts out one of your enemy's eyes. A cyclops, he always misses his target."* ⚠ Flags Greene's passive voice, which deletes whoever chose which suburbs — bombs *"fall short"* and *"land in the less populated suburbs"* as though geography rather than a decision — and that the Reversal completes its law rather than inverting it, the second such in this cluster. concepts.title: Castruccio and Stefano di Poggio
concepts.description: a peaceful man who opposed the conspiracy, correctly predicted a bloodbath, personally prevented one, and was executed with his whole family for asking that it count. **Greene enumerates four forward-facing cards he never played** — money, promises, Roman connections, a brokered marriage. **But the fatal error precedes the appeal**: he disarmed both sides *before* negotiating, so gratitude was what remained after he had given the position away for free. ⚠ The warning was public — Castruccio had already executed *"not an old friend but a new enemy"*; and the invitation to bring the family assembled the targets

concepts.title: Corcyra Versus Corinth at Athens
concepts.description: 433 B.C. Corcyra opens by conceding it has no friendship, no past service, and is there out of fear; offers only a fleet. Corinth gives the brilliant speech and is crushed. **Corinth lost twice** — the gratitude appeal *"only irritated the Athenians"*, and its strategic argument was factually wrong about an Athens that ruled by force and could compel defectors. **The concessions are the mechanism**: they remove the axis on which Corcyra would have lost. ⚠ This is Thucydides, unnamed, and the speeches are his reconstructions

concepts.title: Yelu Ch'u-Ts'ai and the Taxation of China
concepts.description: *"it would be better to exterminate the Chinese and let the grass grow."* A foreigner who had come to value Chinese culture saves it with a **revenue argument**, then saves Kaifeng with an **inventory statement** about craftsmen and engineers. **He never once argued that the thing he was saving was worth saving** — and nothing he said was false. The build's sharpest answer to the book's ethical problem: the identical method produces Duke Wu's executed minister, so **nothing inside it selects the aim**. ⚠ Notes what was conceded — China survived as a tax base — and that Greene misdates the invasion to the twelfth century

concepts.title: Camillus and the Faliscan Schoolmaster
concepts.description: the teacher stripped, bound, and whipped back to the gates by the children he had betrayed, and the city surrenders. **Greene gives the hostages two incompatible values** — enough to divide the city, and *"he had had nothing to lose"* — and the second is operative. **Persuasive force tracks perceived cost, not actual cost.** The whipping is load-bearing, not flourish: restraint alone is ambiguous, and the punishment supplies the verdict that makes surrender thinkable. ⚠ Documented plainly: a man beaten by children, used as an instrument by two parties in succession

concepts.title: Pitch-Pipe Sound Prognostication

concepts.title: The Cloud-Ch'i Reading Doctrine

concepts.title: Cloud-Ch'i Above Cities

concepts.title: Odoshi — The Art of Armor Lacing
concepts.description: the cord that both binds the scales and broadcasts the clan; Kozan's verdict that fine lacing catches the spear it should shed

title: The Bow and the Spear (3)

concepts.title: Kyujutsu — The Art of Archery

concepts.title: Yabusame and Mounted-Archery Rites

concepts.title: Sojutsu and Naginata — The Spear Arts

title: The Sword (4)

concepts.title: Kenjutsu — The Sword Art and Its Schools
concepts.description: the art that refused to be finished; the challenge economy; the orthodox four-target code atop a real practice of any-target deception

concepts.title: Japanese Sword Forging and Blade Aesthetics
concepts.description: the smith-as-priest; the 4.19-million-layer fold; the mekiki/ori-kami appraisal economy; consecration and trade-secrecy as one impulse

concepts.title: Daishō — The Two-Sword Symbolism
concepts.description: the matched pair as the legal badge of caste and the weapon that defends it; the wakizashi as inviolable honor-token; mamori-gatana/gembuku rites

concepts.title: Iaijutsu — The Draw and the Strike
concepts.description: the duel compressed into one uninterruptible instant; killing from rest; the same act as trained readiness or "practice murder" by symmetry alone

title: Secondary Weapon Arts (9)

concepts.title: Kendo — The Modern Sword Discipline

concepts.title: Bajutsu — Military Horsemanship
concepts.description: the horse as an under-armored, hands-free fighting platform engineered for wet, vertical terrain; jobajutsu vs. suibajutsu

concepts.title: Suieijutsu — Swimming in Armor
concepts.description: the art that converts a lethal handicap into the warrior's element; eight schools as a taxonomy of water; stability prized over speed

concepts.title: Tessenjutsu — The War Fan
concepts.description: command baton and iron fan; a weapon that passes a checkpoint by being miscategorized as harmless; the Araki Murashige door-trap

concepts.title: Bojutsu — The Art of the Staff

concepts.title: Jittejutsu — The Police Parrying Weapon
concepts.description: the blunt hook built to trap the katana and take an armed man alive; the no-harm constraint as a higher skill ceiling

concepts.title: Kusarigama and Flexible Chain Weapons
concepts.description: all radius and no core: owns a ring of space, cancelled the instant the enemy crowds inside the arc

concepts.title: Tonfa, Nunchaku, and the Okinawan Farm Weapons
concepts.description: weapon-substitution under disarmament; tools un-confiscatable because the power can't ban the food-implements they hide inside

title: The Empty-Hand Schools (5)

concepts.title: Sumo and Kumiuchi — Grappling
concepts.description: one throw forked two ways: sumo with the killing removed, battlefield kumiuchi with the lethality kept and a dagger added

concepts.title: Aikijutsu and the Daito-ryu Lineage
concepts.description: the institutional genealogy (den-sho, Yoshimitsu→Takeda→Uyeshiba) where a thousand-year lineage's only inspectable link is the last one

concepts.title: Karate — Origins and Schools
concepts.description: the least securely documented striking art and the most confidently traced; the pedigree problem (Bodhidharma retrofitted onto a fight that predates him)

concepts.title: Kappo and Katsu — The Resuscitation Art
concepts.description: the healing twin of atemi; one anatomical map read in two directions; the difference is intent, not knowledge

title: The Tokugawa Control State (7)

concepts.title: Sankin-kotai — The Hostage Control System
concepts.description: the gilded leash: alternate attendance + family hostages + sekisho checkpoints + ruinous processions the lords bankrupt themselves on and call honor

concepts.title: Tokugawa Bakufu Administrative Structure
concepts.description: a machine of engineered distrust: fragmented offices, doubled posts, inspectors wired to watch each other

concepts.title: Daimyo Rank Taxonomy

concepts.title: Gekokujo — The Principle of Displacement

concepts.title: Buke Sho-hatto — Laws of the Military Houses
concepts.description: law as a control instrument aimed inward at the regime's own enforcers; "law must never be violated in favor of reason"

concepts.title: Edo Castle and the Hatamoto Guard
concepts.description: power made physical and legible: concentric moats, trust-by-proximity mansion placement, and the banner-knights who fused guard, governor, and spy

concepts.description: honor-from-below built point-for-point against bushido; defiant of injustice but never revolutionary

concepts.description: the financed, border-crossing, partly-non-Japanese seafaring Japan the samurai story erases; killed by the kaikin, not by force

concepts.description: a force engineered around "take alive"; the non-lethal arsenal and the eta caste absorbing the culture's blood-disgust

concepts.title: Jirocho and Underworld Shadow-Governance
concepts.description: organized crime as shadow state: the gambler/peddler oyabun-kobun hierarchy filling the governance vacuum

title: The Zheng/Qi Duality & Origins (6 built)

concepts.title: The Zheng/Qi Duality — Orthodox and Unorthodox
concepts.description: the core doctrine: engage with the orthodox, win with the unorthodox; the endless mutual-production cycle; qi named first; the I-know-that-you-know regress; the pre-designate (Ts'ao Ts'ao) vs decide-live allocation debate; the unorthodox is a designation in the enemy's mind, not a property of a unit

concepts.title: Ch'i — Etymology of the Unorthodox
concepts.description: a strategic culture built its central war-word from the term for "weird/deviant/odd"; absent from the oracle bones; the drift odd→marvelous→unfathomable→occult; Confucian repression of the strange (Tzu Bu-yü) is why the unorthodox stayed underground; ch'i-mou as the reputed core of PRC thought; qi named first

concepts.title: Formlessness, Vacuity & the Substantial
concepts.description: the form-theory machinery (distinct from the sun-tzu-deception sibling): formless = lacking *predictable* form, reached through facades; the concentrate-vs-fragment 1-vs-10 force-multiplier; manipulate the enemy into vacuities then strike with the whetstone-against-egg

concepts.title: T'ai Kung (Lü Shang) — The Unorthodox Progenitor
concepts.description: the rival origin claim: Shih Chi credits the T'ai Kung, not Sun-tzu; the Mu-yeh 3,000-warrior charge capping decades of preparation; Ch'i as the cradle; the Liu-t'ao post-dates the Art of War, so Sawyer keeps Sun-tzu the conceptual progenitor (progenitor dispute preserved)

concepts.title: The Tso Chuan as Military Progenitor
concepts.description: the manual is downstream of the deed: Li Yüan-ch'un's theory-from-practice thesis (the Art of War abstracted from Tso Chuan battles); read the ancients then create anew imitating nothing; shen-ch'i; the Tso never labels ch'i — the tag is retroactive from the T'ang

concepts.title: Spring & Autumn / Warring States Military Context
concepts.description: the foundational scale page: chariot→mass infantry, the crossbow, armies from ~20k to a million; the war-aim shift from prisoners/plunder to extermination; ritual battle (the li) dies and deception takes over — the unorthodox is a child of scale

title: Spring & Autumn Precursors (10 built)

concepts.title: Ambush & Feigned Retreat
concepts.description: the oldest unorthodox move: a moral trap baited with the enemy's greed (Northern Jung 714 BCE; the diagnosis is of the enemy's *bonds*, not numbers); the make-arrogant-then-strike engine (Ch'u vs Yung 611 BCE); Sun-tzu later warns against the very move

concepts.title: Disguise & Deception
concepts.description: the three earliest faces of deceit: false identity (grain-trader strike on Ku, 520 BCE), false picture (the P'ing-yin dummy-army facade), false story (borrowing passage through Yü, 658–655); the facade only has to survive the enemy's glance, not his scrutiny

concepts.title: Night Maneuvers & Strikes
concepts.description: night dissolves friend-from-foe and real-from-fake; the dusk false-covenant at Shang-mi (635 BCE), the Jao-chiao drumming rout (585), the Li-che River feint; you defeat the enemy's *senses*, not his body — subtract a channel, saturate the rest

concepts.title: Animal Delivery Systems
concepts.description: a weapon family whose payload is terror: fire-elephants (506 BCE), fabricated lions (Tsung Ch'üeh 446 CE), Ti Ch'ing's bronze mask (1040); the tiger-skin "control group" Sawyer flags as showing no overawing effect; a face the enemy can't classify fast enough

concepts.title: Chariot-to-Infantry Conversion (T'ai-yüan, 541 BCE)
concepts.description: Hsün Wu's deer-formation dismount; derision as a tell of laxity ("levity being tantamount to laxity"); Sawyer's restraint — one win is not a military revolution (vs Chao Wu-ling's real one)

concepts.title: The Battle of Ch'eng-p'u (632 BCE)
concepts.description: the paradigm battle: hit the weakest seam (Ch'en/Ts'ai), then a dust-screened feigned retreat draws the strong center onto prepared blades; the 704 BCE Sui anti-model frames it; a feint is only as good as the dust that sells it

concepts.title: The Battle of Chi-fu (519 BCE)
concepts.description: reading a coalition's seams: Ho-lü attacks the members who don't want to be there (Hu/Shen/Chen), spends 3,000 convicts to start the avalanche, attacks on an inauspicious day, and lets freed prisoners carry the panic; a coalition's weakest member is its center of gravity

concepts.title: Wu Tzu-hsü's Exhaustion Strategy
concepts.description: make the bigger enemy break himself: three rotating armies harass Ch'u so it must keep mobilizing, turning its superior size into a liability; strategic enervation + induced misjudgment → the fall of Ying (506 BCE)

concepts.title: Hua Yüan's Night Infiltration
concepts.description: a negotiation won from inside the enemy commander's tent: Hua Yüan climbs onto Tzu Fan's bed ("exchanging our children and eating them") to bargain the siege away (595 BCE); the preserved split — coercive dagger (Tso) vs two honest men trading their exhaustion (Kung Yang / Ho Shou-fa)

concepts.title: Poison, Water & Incendiary Warfare
concepts.description: the birth of environmental warfare: the first poisoning of the Ching River (559 BCE), water-denial, naval/flooding inception, incendiary doctrine; the unorthodox expands the battlefield to the environment itself — the ancient seed of modern infrastructure attack

title: Warring States Commanders & Doctrine (5 built)

concepts.title: Sun Pin — Kuei-ling & Ma-ling
concepts.description: "hit their vacuities": besiege Wei's capital to rescue Chao (the indirect approach); 13 yrs later the cooking-fire deception (100k→50k→30k fires read as desertion) lures P'ang Chüan to the Ma-ling ambush — his own inference kills him

concepts.title: Sun Pin's Unorthodox/Orthodox Philosophy
concepts.description: the philosophical culmination (recovered tomb-text): "when the formless controls the formed, it is unorthodox"; to have FORM is to be nameable and therefore conquerable; "employ the different to create the unorthodox"; singular-control/plural-conquest; melds Sun-tzu's formless with the Tao Te Ching's naming

concepts.title: Pai Ch'i — The Battle of Ch'ang-p'ing
concepts.description: the canonical two-part plan: estrangement (gold + double agents swap the veteran Lien P'o for the "armchair general" Chao Kua; Ch'in secretly installs Pai Ch'i) + the double-unorthodox envelopment that severs Chao's 400,000 from their food; the atrocity-calculus and Pai Ch'i's self-condemning suicide (260 BCE)

concepts.title: The Liu-t'ao's Unorthodox Army
concepts.description: the operational catalogue: segmentation + maneuver as the foundation ("one who cannot divide and move cannot be spoken with about unorthodox stratagems"); the King's Wings general staff; darkness/grass/disguise/forged-orders as means; secrecy ("if fathomed, endangered")

concepts.title: Minor Classics on the Unorthodox
concepts.description: the tradition arguing with itself: the Ssu-ma Fa, Wu-tzu, Wei Liao-tzu (which shrinks the unorthodox to mere sequence, "first orthodox then unorthodox") and Three Strategies compared; the same concept ranges from a throwaway sequencing rule to a cosmology

title: Han Dynasty Realizations (8 built)

concepts.title: Chang Liang & the Yellow-Rock Transmission
concepts.description: the failed-assassin-turned-strategist; the Hsia-p'ei bridge initiation (wisdom-as-arcane-transmission through humility); the hard operational core at Yao-kuan: bribe the butcher-descended generals + fake 50,000 with multiplied flags, then strike the bribe-induced laxity; burn-the-plank-roads as a costly signal

concepts.title: Ch'en P'ing — The Jung-yang Decoy Escape
concepts.description: stack two deceptions to move the enemy twice: 2,000 women-disguised-as-warriors out the west gate, then a double-king's false surrender pulls the besiegers east, opening the real western exit; sacrifice an impostor-self to save the real king (204 BCE). Distinct from the Fan Tseng estrangement

concepts.title: Ch'en P'ing — The P'ai-teng Extrication
concepts.description: reach the enemy commander through a domestic side-channel: exploit the Shan-yü's consort Yen-shih's jealousy (the Han will send beautiful women, displacing her) to lift the Pai-teng siege (200 BCE); Huan T'an's verdict that the secrecy hid the embarrassment, not genius. Distinct from the estrangement page

concepts.title: Stalemate Resolution — Liu Pang vs Hsiang Yü
concepts.description: beat a stronger single enemy by multiplying fronts (run his army ragged) + goad a disciplined enemy's subordinate (Ts'ao Chiu) into the one forbidden mistake; the chest-wound feigned as a foot-wound; the broken truce

concepts.title: Chou Ya-fu — Attritional Defense
concepts.description: "defense as the unorthodox" (154 BCE): when the court expects aggressive rescue, deliberate attrition + sacrificing Liang as bait + sever the supply line + DEFY the emperor's direct order to rescue; the unorthodox is defined against expectation, and here the expectation was action

concepts.title: Fu Chieh-tzu — Assassination Diplomacy
concepts.description: assassination as sanctioned statecraft: the gold-lure draws the covetous Lou-lan king out, the drunken private word, the tent-stabbing, the head carried home; Ssu-ma Kuang's condemnation of the long-term credibility cost the operator discounts

concepts.title: The Red Eyebrows' Bean-Pile Bait
concepts.description: "the illiterate out-deceived the literate" (27 CE): sand mounds skinned with beans as fake provisions bait the famished into self-destructive looting; Feng Yi's counter — a same-uniform ambush that dissolves the enemy's friend-from-foe recognition

concepts.title: Yü Hsü — The Reversed Cooking-Fires
concepts.description: the explicit INVERSION of Sun Pin: *increase* cookfires + march 100 mi/day to project growing strength; the same signal read in opposite directions by relative strength — the deception is the inference you induce, not the gesture (SIGNAL co-anchor)

title: Three Kingdoms Exemplars (8 built)

concepts.title: Sun Ts'e — The Conquest of K'uai-chi
concepts.description: a torch-facade pins the enemy's attention in place while the real force strikes the soft interior at Kao-ch'ien ("seize what they love"); a small-scale echo of Sun Pin's besiege-Wei (196 CE)

concepts.title: Ts'ao Ts'ao — Strategic Profile
concepts.description: the reputation asymmetry: the real innovator (Ch'en Shou: Shang-Yang/Shen-Pu-hai administration + Han-Hsin/Pai-Ch'i unorthodox plots) is remembered as the villain while the mythologized Chu-ko Liang gets the genius-halo; "knowing men / employ despite flaws" as the talent-engine

concepts.title: Ts'ao Ts'ao — The Ma Chao Estrangement
concepts.description: manufacture the war you want (provoke the Kuan-chung generals to concentrate where one blow finishes them) + estrangement by PERSONAL PERFORMANCE: the laughing public meeting with Han Sui + the doctored, erasure-marked letter; the look of collusion does the work (211 CE)

concepts.title: The Battle of Kuan-tu
concepts.description: a single night raid on the supply depot — enabled by the greedy defector Hsü Yu's intelligence + disguise under Yüan Shao's own banners — reverses a hopeless siege; logistics, not the line of battle, was the center of gravity (200 CE)

concepts.title: The Battle of Red Cliffs (Ch'ih Pi)
concepts.description: the commentator who KNEW the warning still swallowed Huang Kai's feigned-surrender fireboats against his lashed fleet (knowing the doctrine grants no immunity); the San-kuo Yen-yi novel-layer inflation (Chu-ko Liang's wind-altar) preserved as a source tension (208 CE)

concepts.title: Lü Meng — The Yi-ling Roadblock
concepts.description: pre-shape the enemy's RETREAT route: fell trees to clog the road first, so his night escape forces a dismount and becomes the kill-zone; the captured 300 horses turn the win into future strength

concepts.title: Chu-ko Tan — The Failed Revolt
concepts.description: the anti-model: bottle 160,000 in one city with no depth/maneuver/second front; Ssu-ma Chao's "Slowness" as the unorthodox — patient encirclement + estrangement agents + the surprise delivered exactly when the enemy concludes you will not attack (257–258 CE)

concepts.title: Teng Ai — The Yin-p'ing March
concepts.description: the impossible-route unorthodox: 700+ miles through deserted mountains, the blanket-roll cliff descent, to overwhelm the enemy's "voids and vacuities"; fatal-terrain turned on his own troops (the beheading-threat) to wring out the last commitment; the end of Shu (263 CE)

title: Northern & Southern Dynasties Commanders (12 built)

concepts.title: Shih Le — The False-Fealty Stratagem
concepts.description: the ex-slave who weaponized his own low status: perform abject submission (hang the rival's letter on the wall, too "awestruck" to read it; "I'm only a barbarian") so the target's vanity does your concealment; then jam the city gates with tribute-cattle and seize him (313–314 CE)

concepts.title: Liu Chü — The Spiritual-Troops Ploy
concepts.description: morale as a manufacturable resource: a shaman's invented omen ("Tzu Ch'an will send spiritual troops") converts terror into aggression; the courage your men lack is supplied by a god you invent (317 CE)

concepts.title: Hsü Tao-fu — Timber-Accumulation Deception
concepts.description: hide a strategic warship-timber stockpile in plain sight by disguising accumulation as cheap commerce, exploiting the fast current so the wood piles up where you want it with no visible hoard for spies to report (410 CE)

concepts.title: Wang Chen-eh — Disinformation River Assault
concepts.description: a small force takes a city by managing what the defenders BELIEVE: a planted rumor (the wrong ally is coming), a phantom rear-army of drums-and-flags, and burning ships as confirming evidence; surprise + disinformation replaces a siege (412 CE)

concepts.title: T'an Tao-chi — Sand as Grain
concepts.description: the Empty-City precursor: sand sacked up and topped with grain fakes abundance, and the enemy's own logic seals it (he beheads his truthful deserters); a calm, unhurried, armorless exit freezes a stronger foe who fears the ambush you don't have (431 CE)

concepts.title: Chü-chao Shih — Crescent & Improvised Weapons
concepts.description: three stacked unorthodox moves under battlefield duress: a mystifying crescent formation that freezes the enemy, weak-bow bait that draws him into range, and spears hacked into giant crossbow-bolts (417 CE)

concepts.title: Fatal-Terrain Actualization Cases
concepts.description: fatal terrain ENGINEERED for your own side: Shen T'ien-tzu's attack-before-encirclement and Wang Chen-eh floating the boats away ("our bones will not return") — irreversibility manufactured on purpose so every man fights as if there is no tomorrow (417 CE)

concepts.title: Ho-pa Yüeh — Feigned Stand-Down
concepts.description: announce a credible delay (the heat, wait for fall) so the enemy disperses himself to farm, then strike the scattered pieces; the released enemy spy carries your lie home and released captives recruit the rest (Northern Wei)

concepts.title: Yü-wen T'ai — Strike the Vanguard
concepts.description: read the enemy commander's emotional state (arrogance, shame, the "resentful army"), exploit his contempt for your past passivity, and decapitate his elite spearpoint so the main body folds; weapons hidden in the grass so the bait looks toothless (537–538 CE)

concepts.title: Ho-juo Tun — Supply Deception
concepts.description: an isolated starving force survives by poisoning the enemy's trust in his own information: fake enough defectors and supply-boats (and boat-fearing horses) that he can no longer accept the real ones, blinding him by exhausting his credulity (558 CE)

concepts.title: Yü-wen Hsien — The Cypress-Hut Facade
concepts.description: a facade of permanence (cypress huts, not tents) buys a clean escape: the enemy hesitates before an empty shell that looks manned, and you are long gone before he tests it ("The Cicada Sheds its Shell," 576 CE)

concepts.title: Chou Fa-shang — False-Defection Ambush
concepts.description: a planted "defector" pre-loads the enemy's belief so the feigned retreat reads as the collapse he was told to expect; then the flag-swap on his own boats steals his refuge and his nerve at once (579 CE)

title: Sui & T'ang Commanders (8 built)

concepts.title: The Sui Conquest of Ch'en
concepts.description: debilitate an enemy over months without a battle: show him decrepitude to breed contempt, build a fake upstream armada to misallocate his troops, and trick him into trading his boats (his one real defense) for useless horses; frozen-sand walls overnight (588–589 CE)

concepts.title: Wei Yün-chi — Barbarians Fight Barbarians
concepts.description: borrow one enemy's trusted relationship with another to get a knife inside the second's guard: 20,000 Turks under a trade-pretext annihilate the unsuspecting Khitan; the deception spends that trust permanently (works once, 605 CE)

concepts.title: Li Mi — Ambush & Enemy Conceit
concepts.description: a victory built on the enemy's NURTURED conceit as much as the hidden troops: let his win-streak and his contempt for "starving brigands" make him reckless, then let his own arrogance walk him onto the ambush (late Sui)

concepts.title: Li Ching — Spiritual Speed
concepts.description: speed that violates the calendar (strike during the flood, when no one expects an army) + knowing when NOT to strike (let fresh ch'i abate) + mercy as a weapon that buys bloodless surrenders (621 CE)

concepts.title: T'ang T'ai-tsung — Black-Armor Special Forces
concepts.description: a small, uniformly fearsome shock-unit + a leader who reads the chi (the incipient moment) and commits at exactly the right instant; intimidation-by-appearance plus impeccable timing, not numbers

concepts.title: Wang Chün — Drums & Disguise Night Strike
concepts.description: at night a tiny force beats a hundredfold enemy by attacking his senses and his trust in his own ranks: disguised infiltrators + drums to the rear convince him he is surrounded, so he kills himself in the dark; "shock and awe" (714 CE)

concepts.title: Kao Hsien-chih — The Pamir Bridge Campaign
concepts.description: a campaign won by controlling thresholds: ford the impossible flood (the enemy never imagines it), stage a friendly welcome to push your own fearful men over the edge, and sever the one rattan bridge so the enemy's relief can never arrive; 72 tribes submit (~747 CE)

concepts.title: Chang Shou-kuei — Assassination by Rival
concepts.description: turn the enemy's internal rivalry into your weapon: find the ambitious rival, let him do the killing, inherit the surrender; but decapitating a leader is not ending the threat — the Khitan power vacuum grew back as the Liao (T'ang)

concepts.title: Questions and Replies — Mutual Transformation

concepts.title: Questions and Replies — All Orthodox, All Unorthodox
concepts.description: the apex teaching: when EVERYTHING is simultaneously orthodox and unorthodox the enemy has no handle at all; "none not orthodox, none not unorthodox"; the labels were a teaching scaffold to be transcended, leaving only formlessness ("give shape to others, be formless ourselves")

concepts.title: Questions and Replies — Vacuity & Substance

concepts.title: Questions and Replies — The Eight Formation

concepts.title: Hu-ch'ien Ching — Contrary Methods
concepts.description: Hsü Tung's (1004 CE) iconoclasm: deliberately contravene the ancient methods to shed predictability ("playing the lute after gluing up the tuning stops"); weaponize the enemy's knowledge of the manual — stage the textbook signs of weakness so the educated enemy reads you per the old book and walks onto the ambush; the Five Differences

concepts.title: Hu-ch'ien Ching — The Eightfold Spy Doctrine
concepts.description: the first text to label subversion/intelligence as "unorthodox" and fold spycraft into it; eight covert-agent methods (converted/double/slander/local agents) + the k'u-jou "suffering flesh" technique — beat your own officer bloody so his "defection" is credible; the self-inflicted wound as the ultimate credibility-signal

concepts.title: Wu-ching Tsung-yao — Unorthodox Troops

concepts.title: The Orthodox/Unorthodox Plasticity Doctrine
concepts.description: **SIGNAL co-anchor:** no force is innately orthodox or unorthodox — the labels are functional, set by role and expectation; and TACTIC-DECAY — a stroke decays from unorthodox to orthodox as it becomes familiar, so every successful surprise plants the seed of its own obsolescence (novelty is a draining charge; the commander is on a treadmill)

concepts.title: Pai-chan Ch'i-lüeh — One Hundred Unorthodox Strategies
concepts.description: the unorthodox systematized as a field guide of 100 paired situations (swiftness/slowness, strong/weak, day/night); a major PLA-reprint revival text; the art is the disciplined choice of which paired option fits the moment

concepts.title: The Ming Great Wall as Unorthodox Defense
concepts.description: the paradox: the most orthodox-looking act (building a wall) reframed as unorthodox because it inverts the expected aggressive posture; the wall as integrated system (strongpoints, forts, watch towers, roving cavalry, military colonies); Mu Ying's Ta-li front-and-back pincer

concepts.title: Ts'ao-lü Ching-lüeh — Essential Strategies from a Grass Hut
concepts.description: the tradition's culmination (152 principles): the unorthodox becomes the ORGANIZING PRINCIPLE of the whole army — segment into ten, make eight of them unorthodox, let the orthodox core merely fix the enemy while the swarm wins; the unorthodox is now the majority, not the exception

concepts.title: T'ou-pi Fu-t'an — The Ten Deceptions
concepts.description: Ho Shou-fa (late Ming): "host and guest have no constant behavior"; the LADDER OF CONCEALMENT — making the enemy misperceive which category is which = victory; making him unaware a category is even in play = "victory within victory"; ten worked deceptions, each with its man

concepts.title: Late-Ch'ing Unorthodox Commentaries

concepts.title: Ch'ien K'un Ta-lüeh — The Decisive Battle

concepts.title: Gilded Age Consolidation Pattern
concepts.description: Same five-step pattern (fragmentation → foundation → crisis → integration → dominance) repeated across steel, oil, railroads, banking. Demonstrates consolidation is structural, not genius-dependent. Enabling conditions: capital availability, crisis frequency, low antitrust enforcement, scale advantages. Implication: consolidation predictable when conditions align.

concepts.title: Industrial Consolidation as Selection
concepts.description: Consolidation driven by structural selection environment. Selection pressure: cost structure (primary), capital strength (secondary), managerial excellence (tertiary). Example: steel 1870-1900, dozens fragmented → 1893 crisis selects for fitness → Carnegie emerges dominant.

concepts.title: Civil War as Capital Redistribution
concepts.description: Civil War created capital accumulation conditions enabling Carnegie's 1860s wealth. Military demand surge + post-war reconstruction + cheap labor. War-era capital enabled 1872 entry into steel, compressing passive income timeline from ~1880s to 1872.

concepts.title: Recession Consolidation
concepts.description: Recessions function as selection filters: Collapse (weak fail), Survive Weakened (moderate shrink), Consolidate & Expand (strong with capital reserves win). 1873 and 1893 panics: Carnegie with capital reserves survived and consolidated; competitors without reserves collapsed or sold.

title: Thucydides Trap Recognition (1 page)

concepts.title: Thucydides Trap Recognition
concepts.description: Dominant power recognizes rising power and accommodates via exit/cooperation. Carnegie recognized Morgan's threat (1899-1900), exited at premium ($480M) rather than fighting U.S. Steel. Strategic accommodation preserved capital for philanthropy and reputation. Fighting the trap leads to worse outcomes.
